correctness.rationale: The prime-power formula makes every non-squarefree n impossible. For squarefree n with two primes, parity and the bound on (P(n)+1)/n force one exact quotient and an impossible factor equation. For three primes, the even case forces quotient 5 and the odd case quotient 6. The resulting equations are exhausted, including the small boundary pairs before the monotone inequalities apply. No finite experiment is used to justify the universal conclusion.

value.rationale: The original iff-prime conjecture is now false, making the structural location of the first possible composite failures mathematically natural. The theorem proves that every composite failure is squarefree and needs at least four distinct prime factors, completely resolving the full Omega<=3 layer. This is an infinite structural restriction on the exact historical congruence rather than a bounded search.
